name: Barry Moore

issue_poll.name: Cygnal / Gray Media Alabama / Alabama Daily News poll of 500 likely general-election voters, Oct 16-17, 2026 (most important issue)
issue_poll.note: Single state poll ranking most important issue; top 10 taken in poll order (abortion and gun control ranked 11-12).

issues.detail: Lower inflation by cutting federal spending and ending new money creation; tariffs and domestic production
Total ban on stock trading by members of Congress, extended to all politicians
Pass Americans First Immigration Act codifying five Trump immigration orders; deport all illegal immigrants; English as official language
No tax increases ever; replace income tax with FairTax; pass all 12 appropriations bills individually; cut foreign aid
Use tariffs as leverage to reshore production; cut regulations; recruit employers to Alabama
Oppose extending enhanced ACA subsidies; allow insurance sales across state lines; no new federal health programs beyond Medicare/Medicaid
Prioritize federal prosecution of antifa groups and violent criminals; fully fund law enforcement
Expand I-65 to six lanes (stated top priority)
Eliminate the U.S. Department of Education and return control to states; bar foreign government funding of U.S. education

plan_caveats: Campaign issues page (barrymooreforalabama.com/issues) could not be fetched; homepage summary and Branch Politics profile used instead.

No general-election debate was held and Moore declined WSFA/APR interview requests; he repeatedly told voters to judge him on his House record rather than promises, so few forward-looking specifics exist.
Inflation rated Partial (named mechanism: spending cuts) rather than Vague; judgment call.
Health care rated Partial because his opposition to extending enhanced ACA subsidies was hedged ('probably never', unless major reforms); Dec 2025 radio remarks as a declared Senate candidate.
Education and FairTax positions come from his 2026 Senate iVoterGuide questionnaire ('strongly agree' answers), not speeches.
Crime: his Sept 2025 op-ed backing House-passed DC crime bills was treated as House record, not a Senate promise.
Data centers: no Moore statement found; source URL shows a BCA event on the topic where no Moore position was reported.
